items.t: Enbridge stock: Line 3 stake talks target C$1.5 billion deal
sum: Enbridge stock is in focus after talks emerged over a possible minority sale in the company's Line 3 crude oil pipeline network. Stockwatch, citing The Globe and Mail, reported on Thursday, November 26, that a consortium of Indigenous communities is in talks with Enbridge over a potential transaction.
The reported proposal involves more than three dozen First Nations and Metis communities. The consortium is seeking a 6 percent interest in Line 3 for about C$1.5 billion, according to the report.

Line 3 runs from Edmonton, Alberta, to Superior, Wisconsin, and can transport up to 760,000 barrels of crude oil per day. It is part of Enbridge's mainline system, described by Stockwatch as North America's largest oil pipeline network, with capacity of up to 3 million barrels per day.

Enbridge declined to comment on potential Line 3 investments, while saying it is exploring financial partnerships across numerous assets where the economics are favorable for Indigenous partners and the company. The reported Line 3 transaction is slated to be announced in early 2027, but the talks do not establish that a sale will be completed.

For investors, the development highlights a possible ownership change in a core liquids-pipeline asset and a broader push to involve Indigenous communities in Canadian energy infrastructure. The eventual structure, valuation and timing would remain key factors for Enbridge's capital allocation and partnership strategy.

sum: Although many investors are fretting over what to do with their artificial intelligence stocks amid the recent volatility surrounding Nvidia Corp. (NVDA-Q), money manager Rebecca Teltscher is comfortable sitting on the sidelines with her portfolio of Canadian dividend companies.

“We’re okay to not participate in very risky sectors or stocks, even if that means giving up some upside return, as long as we’re protecting [our clients] on the downside,” says Ms. Teltscher, partner and portfolio manager at Newhaven Asset Management Inc. in Toronto, which oversees about $510-million in assets.

“Most of our clients are not necessarily interested in beating the benchmarks,” she says. “They’re really just looking to maintain their lifestyle in retirement and grow it at [the rate of] inflation.”

For example, she says a $2-million portfolio with a modest 4-per-cent dividend yield could generate about $80,000 in income annually. Canadian dividends also receive favourable tax treatment, Ms. Teltscher notes.

Her team’s portfolio has returned 19.8 per cent year-to-date and 23.1 per cent over the past 12 months. Its three- and five-year annualized returns were 22.9 per cent and 12.6 per cent, respectively. The performance is based on total returns, net of fees, as of Nov. 30.
The Globe spoke with Ms. Teltscher recently about what she’s been buying and selling:

Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. (AEM-T), the Toronto-based gold miner, is a stock we’ve held for several years and have been adding to recently on a dip. We usually add more when it falls to the low-$200-a-share range. It’s the only gold company we own – or mining company, for that matter.

Enbridge vs. Canadian Natural Resources: Where to Invest Your Next $5,000
sum: The Canadian energy sector is correcting, and investors are wondering which stock to invest in next. At the top of the energy sector are Enbridge (TSX: ENB) and Canadian Natural Resources (TSX: CNQ). They have the advantage of low costs and are due to announce their 2027 dividend growth rate, which makes them a buy-and-hold for the long term.

Both stocks are down more than 18% from their 2026 peak and have been in a downtrend since October, when US mid-term elections changed the market’s perspective. They cater to different aspects of the energy sector, which brings different risk exposure.
Canadian Natural Resources produces, refines, and sells oil and natural gas. Thus, its share price is influenced by oil and natural gas prices.

The US-Iran war kept oil prices closer to $100 for most of 2026. However, things could ease in 2027 as the Middle East adjusts to higher shipping costs. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts the Brent crude price to fall from US$93 at present to US$78/barrel in December and then settle at an average price of US$88/barrel in 2027.

A further dip in oil prices could pull down CNQ stock price to probably $59, inflating its dividend yield to 4.3% from 3.9% at present. The company could grow its dividend by an average annual rate of 10% as it sticks to the financial model.

Enbridge has been investing heavily in pipeline infrastructure. This has increased its net debt to 5.1 times adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA), beyond its target range of 4.5–5.0 times. This target could be achieved in 2027 once the upcoming acquisitions and newly commissioned projects increase EBITDA. The company has also raised $3 billion in equity financing.

High leverage and equity dilution make investors wonder if Enbridge will accelerate its dividend growth rate to 5% in 2027 or retain it at 3%. Management retained its 2027 guidance of a 5% increase in distributable cash flow (DCF), but that may not convert to 5% dividend growth as the company uses more of its cash flow to self-fund its projects.

sum: While Enbridge (TSX: ENB) is a Canadian behemoth, Pembina Pipeline (TSX: PPL) is a peer pipeline company that is much smaller in size.
Pipelines are similar to toll roads as they charge a fee to move oil and gas. So, compared to upstream oil companies, pipeline stocks benefit from a steady stream of cash flow.

Over the last 20 years, ENB stock has returned 750% to shareholders after adjusting for dividend reinvestments. Comparatively, PPL stock has generated cumulative returns totaling 1,450% over this period.

Greg Ebel ended his last Enbridge (TSX: ENB) earnings call with a comment calling himself “a forever shareholder.” Ebel retires at year-end, yet he is still betting on the company he spent four years shaping.

Enbridge stock: Wexpro secures approval for US dollar 485 million deal
sum: Wexpro, an Enbridge company, received approval on November 18, 2026, from the public service commissions of Utah and Wyoming for its acquisition of Laramie Energy's Colorado natural gas assets. Enbridge put the transaction's value at 485 million US dollars, with up to 65 million US dollars in contingent payments.

The deal includes Laramie Energy's assets in Colorado's Piceance Basin. Wexpro operates as an exploration and production business that supplies natural gas to Enbridge's utility operations at cost of service rather than selling all production at market prices.

Enbridge said the acquisition will increase the share of gas supplied by Wexpro to customers of Enbridge Gas Utah, Wyoming and Idaho. Wexpro currently supplies about 40 percent of the gas consumed by those customers from roughly 550 producing wells, mainly in Wyoming.

The arrangement is designed to give the utility a more stable source of natural gas while reducing customer exposure to commodity-price volatility. For Enbridge, the transaction adds producing assets to a business model linked to regulated utility demand and cost-of-service returns.

The company also said the assets will extend Wexpro's operating footprint across parts of Wyoming, Colorado and Utah. That gives the acquisition a broader regional role than a standalone production purchase, although the source did not provide a separate earnings forecast for the assets.

Enbridge vs. Telus: Which Stock Offers More Reliable Income Through 2030?
sum: If you’re looking for Canadian dividend stocks that can keep paying you for years, Enbridge (TSX: ENB) and Telus (TSX: T) are two names you’ve almost certainly considered.
Both own massive infrastructure networks and provide essential services, giving them businesses that can generate recurring revenue through different economic conditions.

However, when you’re building a portfolio for the long haul and looking for reliable stocks that can earn you attractive returns through at least 2030, there’s more to consider than whether customers will still need those services.
After all, companies also need to maintain their assets, manage their debt and keep investing in growth while returning some of those earnings to shareholders.

So, although Enbridge and Telus are two of the top long-term stocks to buy and hold at the core of your portfolio, and both offer attractive dividends, here’s which stock gets the slight edge when it comes to reliability over the next few years.

There’s no question that telecom stocks can be some of the best dividend stocks to buy and hold for the long haul. In fact, Telus currently yields roughly 5%, thanks to its massive wireless and internet business serving millions of Canadians.

Those services remain essential, and its established networks give it a significant competitive advantage. However, after years of heavy spending on fibre, 5G infrastructure and acquisitions, the company was left with considerable debt and a dividend that was consuming too much cash.

How Many Enbridge Shares You Need for $1,000 in Dividends
sum: Greg Ebel is walking away on his own terms as the CEO of Enbridge (TSX: ENB). On November 6, Ebel delivered his final earnings call message and called himself “a forever shareholder.” Incoming CEO Michele Harradence also told analysts that her family members have owned shares since the company’s 1953 IPO.

Valued at a market cap of $153 billion, Enbridge is an energy infrastructure giant that has created inflation-beating returns for long-term investors. Despite its stellar returns, ENB stock offers you a dividend yield of 5.8% in November 2026.
So here is the question worth asking. What would it take to start your own Enbridge income stream? Let’s work it out with real numbers.

Enbridge transports oil and natural gas across North America. It also runs gas utilities that serve homes and businesses, plus a renewable power business with long-term contracts. Ebel said Enbridge is the largest transporter of liquids on the continent.

A diversified portfolio of cash-generating assets allows Enbridge to pay and increase dividends across business cycles. The blue-chip dividend stock has raised dividends for 31 consecutive years. In 2026, Enbridge raised the payout by 3% to $0.97 per share per quarter or $3.88 per year.

Enbridge stock trades at $68.59 and pays $3.88 per share each year. Divide $1,000 by $3.88, and you get around 258 shares. At $68.59, those 258 shares cost about $17,696, which will pay $1,000 each year or $250 per quarter.
If Enbridge keeps raising its payout 3% a year, those 258 shares would pay about $1,160 in five years. Notably, the annual dividend has risen from $0.58 per share in 2006.

BCE vs. Enbridge: Which Stock Offers the More Convincing Dividend Case?
sum: Two dividend yields can sit side by side on a screen and look close enough to flip a coin. One business could be spending heavily to repair its finances while the other has room to raise its cheque. I'd rather find out which is which before handing either of them my retirement money.

An internet provider and a pipeline owner both operate expensive networks. Customers can keep paying while the company spends heavily on repairs, upgrades and interest. The dividend depends on what's left after the bills that keep the business going.

Free cash flow (FCF) measures cash available after certain spending. Companies can define it differently, which is why I'd compare each business with its own prior periods and its own payout. The biggest dollar amount on the page doesn't tell me which cheque has more breathing room.

My first check after a dividend reset is whether the company is putting the extra cash to work in a way I can see. Paying down debt can lower the interest bill over time. Network investment can earn its keep if customers sign up and stay. Yet both take longer than changing the number on a dividend declaration.

A company that cuts its dividend can become a better investment if the cash it keeps reduces debt or improves the business. Therefore give it credit as those benefits show up. Until then, I'd look at the new payout and avoid building the plan around what it used to pay.

BCE (TSX: BCE) earns from wireless, internet and other communications services. Its third-quarter operating cash flow rose to $2.2 billion, while company-defined free cash flow fell to $854 million from about $1 billion a year earlier. The gap is a reminder that keeping and expanding the network takes real money.

Enbridge (TSX: ENB) earns from its oil and gas pipelines and natural gas utilities. It reaffirmed 2026 distributable cash flow guidance of $5.70 to $6.10 per share. That's a company measure of the cash available after certain costs, and the $3.88 annualized dividend takes about two-thirds of the midpoint.

sum: Enbridge столкнулся с более низким прогнозом прибыли от Scotiabank на неделе с 9 по 13 ноября, в то время как в отдельном отчете указано, что финансирование облигаций на сумму 3,2 миллиарда долларов США запланировано к поставке в пятницу, 13 ноября. Эти события добавляют осторожности аналитикам и финансовой активности к недавнему квартальному отчету канадской энергетической инфраструктурной группы.

В пятницу, 13 ноября, MarketBeat сообщил, что Scotiabank понизил оценку прибыли Enbridge в отчете, опубликованном в среду, 11 ноября. Банк снизил свой прогноз с 2,08 до 2,04 доллара США на акцию и сохранил рекомендацию «Сильная покупка».

Пересмотренный прогноз оказался ниже консенсус-оценки, приведенной MarketBeat. Это изменение последовало за результатами Enbridge за третий квартал от 6 ноября, которые, как говорится в отчете, превысили консенсус-прогноз квартальной прибыли.

Krugman Insights сообщила в пятницу, 13 ноября, что Enbridge назначила сделку на сумму 3,2 млрд долларов США, охватывающую пять траншей старших и фиксированных субординированных облигаций. В отчете указано, что финансирование находится в стадии реализации, поэтому запланированную поставку не следует путать с завершенной сделкой.

Для инвесторов сочетание снижения прогноза внешних доходов и новой финансовой деятельности привлекает внимание к траектории доходов Enbridge, потребностям в капитале и управлению балансом. Эти два события касаются разных частей инвестиционного проекта: одно меняет ожидания аналитиков, а другое касается финансирования операций и проектов компании.

Последние события произошли после того, как Enbridge подтвердила свой годовой прогноз, опубликовав результаты за третий квартал. Аналитический пересмотр сам по себе не означает изменения в руководстве компании, в то время как отчет по облигациям описывает условия и сроки финансирования, а не изменение операционных целей.

Далее участники рынка сосредоточат свое внимание на результатах деятельности компании в сравнении с ее прогнозами, расходами на проект и затратами на финансирование. Сектор энергетической инфраструктуры Канады остается актуальным для более широких текущих рыночных отчетов.

In its earnings release, the Canadian energy infrastructure group said adjusted EBITDA reached CAD 4.434 billion for the three months ended September 30, compared with CAD 4.267 billion a year earlier. The company said its secured growth backlog stood at approximately CAD 38 billion after more than CAD 3 billion of gas transmission projects entered service during the quarter. Enbridge is targeting CAD 10 billion to CAD 20 billion of new project announcements through 2027 and expects annual growth investment capacity of CAD 10 billion to CAD 11 billion.

sum: We just published our list of the 10 Stocks I Am Retiring On, and Enbridge Inc. (NYSE:ENB) ranked 10th on the list.

A retirement portfolio needs businesses that can keep rewarding shareholders long after the current market narrative fades. Dividends show how important those quieter sources of return can be: according to S&P Dow Jones Indices research cited in our coverage of Dividend Aristocrat stocks, dividends have accounted for roughly 31% of the S&P 500's total return since 1926, with capital appreciation accounting for the remaining 69%. In the 1940s and 1970s, dividend income accounted for more than half of total returns. The lesson is not that every retirement investment must pay dividends, but rather that long-term shareholder gains can come from sources other than rising share prices.

Warren Buffett offers a useful test for that level of dedication. He has advised investors to buy only what they would "perfectly happy to hold if the market shut down for 10 years." Rather than relying on the potential to sell tomorrow, investors should consider how much the underlying business may make over a decade. That business-owner perspective is the common thread running through Insider Monkey's discussion of Warren Buffett's best long-term stocks to buy.

For retirement investors, the distinction between a high starting dividend and an increasing dividend is crucial. The S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index requires components to have increased dividends for at least 25 years in a row. This is a record that spans numerous economic cycles, though it doesn't guarantee future growth. Insider Monkey's analysis of dividend growth stocks to buy and hold in 2026 looked at 68 such companies and evaluated their five-year average dividend growth rates.

Of course, financial strength is just as important as payout record. A dividend competes with debt repayments, capital spending, and other financial requirements. Liabilities are broader than debt, but the comparison shows the type of liquidity cushion worth considering alongside dividend yield.

Enbridge earned its place on the list after The Motley Fool's Matt DiLallo named it a stock he planned to buy in his retirement account, while Seeking Alpha's Leo Nelissen included it in his 20-stock model retirement portfolio.

How Much Would You Need to Invest in Enbridge to Average $200 a Month?
sum: A company helping deliver energy to your home can also help pay the bills. The appealing part is getting cash without selling shares every month. The less attractive part is building the holding first. At the current payment and recent closing price, roughly $42,600 in one pipeline stock could produce a $200 monthly average, with the cash arriving quarterly.

A $200 monthly average means $2,400 a year. For a stock paying every three months, the practical target is about $600 each quarter. I’d collect the dividends in cash and make monthly transfers from that balance, giving my spending a smoother schedule than the company’s payment calendar.

Enbridge (TSX: ENB) makes that calculation possible with a quarterly dividend of $0.97 per share. Its annualized $3.88 payment yields about 5.6% at the recent closing price of $68.82. That’s substantial starting income, so the next step is making sure the business has room to pay it.

Enbridge operates oil and natural gas pipelines, gas utilities, and other energy infrastructure. Much of its earnings relies on regulated returns or contracted service, giving it a different relationship with oil prices from a producer selling the commodity. Customers pay for access to infrastructure they need to move and use energy.

Utilities and export facilities needing more gas capacity offer growth opportunities. Enbridge’s second-quarter update described new pipeline connections and expansions supported by customer demand. New assets can add earnings once operating, although construction spending comes before those earnings arrive.

For the dividend, management reaffirmed 2026 distributable cash flow of $5.70 to $6.10 per share. This is the company’s cash-flow measure after adjustments including maintenance spending and financing costs. The $3.88 annual dividend uses roughly 64% to 68% of that range, leaving some cash beyond the payment.
Reaching at least $2,400 annually requires 619 whole shares at the current payment. Using the recent close, and excluding trading fees, here’s the investment required.

items.t: Inflation Is Heading to 3.5%: Yet These 2 Canadian Stocks Can Raise Prices and Keep Their Customers
sum: Canadians do not need a spreadsheet to know that prices are on the rise. They notice these trends at the pump and the grocery checkout.

Statistics Canada reported that consumer prices rose 3.1% year over year in September, up from 3.0% in August. On October 28, the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.50%, its first hike since July 2023.
The central bank also expects inflation to reach about 3.5% by the end of 2026. Moreover, the regulator does not see a return to its 2% target until mid-2028.
Given this macro backdrop, let’s see which companies are well positioned to pass higher costs to customers.
The Bank of Canada says inflation excluding gasoline was 2.2% in September, and the core measure remains close to 2%.
However, the central bank says high fuel prices are lifting production and transportation costs, which have been primarily absorbed by businesses.
Notably, companies that do not enjoy pricing power have seen profit margins shrink over the last six months.

Here’s Where Enbridge Stock Could Be Headed in the Next 3 Years
sum: Enbridge (TSX: ENB) has been on a roll for the past 30 months. Investors who missed the rebound are wondering if ENB stock is still undervalued and good to buy for a self-directed Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) or Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) portfolio focused on dividends and total returns.
Enbridge trades near $72.50 per share at the time of writing. The stock was as low as $43 in late 2023 and isn’t far off the recent record high above $77.

In order to get a sense of where the stock might be headed in the next few years, it is important to look at the reason the stock pulled back through the second half of 2022 and most of 2023 before reversing course.

Investors will recall that the Bank of Canada and the U.S. Federal Reserve started to raise interest rates in 2022 and continued the rate increases through 2023 in an effort to get inflation under control. Enbridge and its energy infrastructure peers use debt to fund growth investments, including acquisitions and capital projects. The steep rise in borrowing costs that occurred over such a short period of time caused concern among investors who worried that a spike in debt expenses would hurt profits and cut into cash flow that could be used to reduce debt and pay dividends. Some pundits even speculated that Enbridge’s generous dividend would be at risk of being cut to preserve cash.

The recovery in the share price began around the time the central banks indicated they were done raising interest rates. Bargain hunters moved into the stock, anticipating rate cuts in 2024 and 2025. These reductions materialized, helping push ENB even higher.

Earlier this year, the market broadly expected additional rate cuts for 2026. That might not happen as soaring oil prices are putting upward pressure on inflation. Analysts are now starting to warn that rate increases might be needed in Canada and the United States if inflation jumps in the coming months. In that scenario, Enbridge’s stock price would face new headwinds.
Enbridge is offsetting the impact of higher interest rates by growing revenue and earnings. The company spent US$14 billion in 2024 to buy three American natural gas utilities.

Suncor, Enbridge, or Canadian Natural — Which Oil Stock Fits Your Portfolio Best?
sum: Canadian oil stocks used to be a filthy asset class. However, since 2020, these stocks have steadily been gaining popularity with both retail and institutional investors.

In the past five years, the sector has significantly consolidated and outperformed. The best producers drastically reduced debt and cleaned up their balance sheets. Likewise, they focused on the most economic assets and drilling opportunities.

As result, Canadian oil stocks are lean, cash flow machines. Since the Iran war pushed oil prices skyward, Canadian oil stocks are set to enjoy a major windfall. Suncor Enbridge (TSX: SU), Enbridge (TSX: ENB), and Canadian Natural Resources (TSX: CNQ) are some of Canada’s best known energy stocks. Here’s why each has its investment merits and why you might want to prefer one over the other.

With a market cap of $104 billion, Suncor Energy is Canada’s top integrated oil stock. It produces 855,000 barrels of oil per day and refines 466,000 barrels of oil per day. It also has a large retail distribution network through 1,640 Petro-Canada retail locations and 320 commercial Cardlock locations.
Suncor’s stock lagged for several years due to underperforming operations and safety issues. However, its new management has largely cleaned up the business.

With a strong balance sheet today and a mix of long-life assets (25 years of reserves), Suncor has committed to returning 100% of its excess cash flows to shareholders. It has also committed to growing its dividend by 3-5% per year. It yields 2.73% today.
This is a good stock if you want a diversified mix of assets that generate strong cash flows. While this oil stock has a lower yield, capital returns will come as it steadily retires its share count.

This Energy Stock Pays a 5.8% Dividend (And It's Safe)
sum: - The pipeline and utility company has very conservative financial metrics.
- It has plenty of fuel to invest in growing its operations while continuing to increase its high-yielding dividend.
Enbridge (NYSE: ENB) entered 2026 with a 5.8% dividend yield. That's several times higher than the S&P 500's yield, which is near a record low at around 1.1%.
While higher-yielding dividend stocks can have a higher risk profile, that's not the case with Enbridge. Its high-yielding dividend is very safe.
Enbridge has paid dividends for more than 70 years. The company recently announced plans to increase its payment by 3% for 2026, marking its 31st consecutive year of dividend raises.

The Canadian pipeline and utility company generates very stable and predictable cash flow. Roughly 98% of its cash flows come from cost-of-service agreements or long-term, fixed-fee contracts. Enbridge's earnings are so predictable that it has achieved its annual financial guidance for 19 years in a row.

Enbridge pays out 60%-70% of its stable cash flow in dividends, enabling it to retain billions of dollars annually. The company also has a strong investment-grade balance sheet, backed by a leverage ratio within its target range of 4.5-5.0 times. As a result, Enbridge has ample financial flexibility to fund organic expansion projects and make bolt-on acquisitions.
